exercises.instruction: Find six pairs of words which have a similar meaning.
Agree with the opinions below using a word with the same meaning. The first two letters of each answer are given.
items: 1 A: She's always wanted to get to the top in her career, hasn't she?
2 A: She was horrible, wasn't she?
3 A: He's happy and smiling whenever you see him.
B: I know, he's always very ch.......................... .
4 A: The problem is that she can't change any of her ideas and adapt to new ones.
5 A: Do you honestly think we can depend on that old car of yours?
B: No, it's very un.......................... – it could break down at any time.
6 A: He never thinks about other people's feelings, does he?

exercises.instruction: Write an opposite for each of these words. Three of them just require a prefix (e.g. un-; dis-); the other three need a completely different word. Look at the examples first.
Fill the gaps in the text with suitable words from the box. (There are more words in the box than you need.)
items: I spent the weekend camping with friends but it wasn't very successful. Sally is not very (1).......................... and we had to wait an hour for her to turn up. Apparently she had a problem with the train, but didn't have the common (2).......................... to ring me on my mobile and warn me she would be late. Then, when she finally arrived, she had a friend with her, called Jill. She was quite nice, but so (3).......................... that she didn't really speak to anyone for the first day. She'd got a bit more self- (4).......................... by the end of the weekend. However, she didn't seem to have much (5)..........................: we were only 400 metres from a farm but Jill said she couldn't make tea because we had no water! Bill got angry at that, for no real reason, and poor Jill almost started crying. Bill's problem was that he never really wanted to go camping in the first place, so he was pretty (6).......................... most of the time.
